chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When the Imam attends the funeral, he is more entitled than the people to pray over it."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: Prayer (specifically Salat al-Janazah, the funeral prayer)
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: The Imam, referring to the religious leader or the one leading the prayer

ai.seo_question: Who has the right to lead the funeral prayer if the Imam is present?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the hierarchical structure of communal worship in Shia jurisprudence, affirming the Imam's (or Caliph's) prerogative to lead the funeral prayer as a symbol of political and religious authority. While the presence of the Imam grants him precedence, scholars note that this does not invalidate the validity of the prayer if others lead in his absence, reflecting the balance between ritual correctness and social order. The ruling highlights the Imam's role as the primary intercessor and leader for the community in both life and death.
